modes.partial: One call per batch, sum first 32 of 64 (528)
modes.retained: Two calls per batch; sum both 1..64 streams and reread the first value of the initial retained iterator (4161)

sampling: 1, 16 or 256 batches in one process; three separate measured processes per case, after raw interpreter and uninstrumented native output agreement. Checkpoints precede each new request-stream allocation. Counters start after constant initialization. Final counters follow root execution, joining its child tasks and cached-value cleanup, before whole-runtime shutdown. Reusable connections and detached I/O tasks are still live at this point.
limits: Collection disabled, physical freeing enabled. Compared with the retained repeated-call baseline using the same source programs, input sizes and output checks. Managed allocation/count totals and explicit request/message releases are measured before whole-runtime shutdown. Constant final managed charge is required in every measured mode and size, as is release of all created streams and queued messages. Reusable connections and detached I/O tasks remain live at the final sampling point; their remaining storage is not a demonstrated leak. Partial readers can avoid constructing later messages once abandoned, so message-construction work can differ. Other raw buffers, allocator/TLS/OS storage, server/process memory and timing are excluded. Connections and retained callback graphs still require tracing; these cases do not establish unlimited-call bounds, checked ARC, zero-cost abstractions or C/Rust parity. This compiler comparison requires fewer retains in every measured case without extra allocation requests or higher final managed storage; shared records keep their existing owners. Dynamic dispatch, record allocations and ownership tests remain.

hosts.scope: One native client process makes 1, 16 or 256 batches of remote calls over loopback HTTP/2 to an interpreted greeter. Each response contains integers 1..64. Full batches sum all 64; partial batches sum only the first 32; retained batches sum an initial stream, make and sum a second call while retaining the initial iterator, then reread its first value. Retained batches therefore make twice as many calls. Raw unoptimized interpreter and ordinary native output must agree. Three separate instrumented processes per case count managed allocations/retains/charged bytes, created/finalized connection and stream objects, and requested/freed queued-message bytes including their header and trailing byte. GC is disabled, physical freeing enabled. Counters start after constant initialization. Final counters follow root execution, joining its child tasks and cached-value cleanup, before whole-runtime shutdown. Reusable connections and detached I/O tasks are still live; the sample does not establish their destruction. Checkpoints are immediately before each new stream is allocated, after connection selection and request-header preparation; a checkpoint can deliberately include an earlier retained iterator. Excludes other raw buffers, TLS/OS/allocator metadata, server/whole-process memory and timing. Native builds use ordinary -O2. Source, generated C, executables and raw stderr are retained.
